{{Short description|Circles related to a point in the plane}}
{{Distinguish|Tangent lines to circles}}

In [[geometry]], '''tangent circles''' (also known as '''kissing circles''') are circles in a common plane that intersect in a single point.  There are two types of [[tangent|tangency]]: internal and external.  Many problems and constructions in geometry are related to tangent circles; such problems often have real-life applications, such as [[trilateration]] and maximizing the use of materials.

==Two given circles==
[[File:Locus of centers of circles tangent to two circles.gif|thumb|right|[[Ellipse]] and [[hyperbola]] as the [[locus (mathematics)|locus]] of centers of circles tangent to two given intersecting circles.]]
Two circles are mutually and externally tangent if the distance between their centers is equal to the sum of their radii.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Tangent Circles |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/TangentCircles.html |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Three given circles: Apollonius' problem==

{{main|Problem of Apollonius}}

Apollonius' problem is to construct circles that are tangent to three given circles.

===Apollonian gasket===

{{main|Apollonian gasket}}

If a circle is iteratively inscribed into the interstitial curved triangles between three mutually tangent circles, an Apollonian gasket results, one of the earliest fractals described in print.
[[File:Pythagorean_triple_kissing_circles.svg|thumb|Three mutually tangent circles of radii in ratios 4:4:1 yield a 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple triangle]]

==Malfatti's problem==

{{main|Malfatti circles}}

Malfatti's problem is to carve three cylinders from a triangular block of marble, using as much of the marble as possible. In 1803, [[Gian Francesco Malfatti]] conjectured that the solution would be obtained by inscribing three mutually tangent circles into the triangle (a problem that had previously been considered by Japanese mathematician [[Ajima Naonobu]]); these circles are now known as the [[Malfatti circles]], although the conjecture has been proven to be false.

==Six circles theorem==

{{main|Six circles theorem}}

A chain of six circles can be drawn such that each circle is tangent to two sides of a given triangle and also to the preceding circle in the chain. The chain closes; the sixth circle is always tangent to the first circle.

==Generalizations==

Problems involving tangent circles are often generalized to spheres.  For example, the Fermat problem of finding sphere(s) tangent to four given spheres is a generalization of [[problem of Apollonius|Apollonius' problem]], whereas [[Soddy's hexlet]] is a generalization of a [[Steiner chain]].

* [[Arbelos]], a shape formed by three tangent circles, one outside the other two
* [[Archimedean circle]], additional circles associated with and sometimes tangent to an arbelos
* [[Ring lemma]], on the radii of a ring of tangent circles surrounding a central circle
